_meta.purpose: The durable list of OPEN leads. A lead recorded only in a chat transcript is lost at the next compaction, and a lead recorded only in gen_prompts.py cannot be checked -- nothing in the fleet reports which queue item a job took, so a lead that was tried and failed looks identical to one nobody ever attempted. Each entry below carries a WITNESS: a grep against the live seed tree that matches WHILE THE LEAD IS STILL OPEN. Run check_leads.py to turn 'do we remember this?' into 'is it still in the tree?'.
_meta.usage:
python3 check_leads.py            # status of every lead
python3 check_leads.py --open     # only the ones still open
_meta.status_values: open = witness still matches, nobody has landed it. landed = witness gone, RE-PRICE THE SIBLINGS. unverifiable = no mechanical witness exists; must be checked by hand.
_meta.rule: When a lead flips to landed, do not just delete it -- the pattern that paid once is a reason to CHECK the next instance, never a reason to assume it. Re-derive the siblings against the new tree before requeueing them.
_meta.trees: THREE tree locations, NOT interchangeable. records/<slug>/ is the LEADER's tree, reseeded from whoever holds the record -- this is what jobs are seeded from and therefore what a lead must beat. projs/<slug>/Solution/ is OUR working tree; it equals records/ only on slugs where we lead (on keccak-f1600 ours is theta 3200 against the record's 2240, so reading the wrong one INVERTS the answer). out/<slug>/ is per-job scratch, wiped and re-extracted for the very next job -- a constant read there belongs to whichever job landed last. check_leads.py resolves records/ then projs/ then out/, in that order.
_meta.price_zero: price 0 means UNPRICED, not worthless -- a lead whose mechanism is confirmed but whose row count has not been derived. Derive it before queueing, and write the number back here. Only fb-queue-stale is genuinely a 0 (it is queue hygiene).
_meta.fixed_challenge_rule: THE FIXED-CHALLENGE VACUITY RULE. Our soundness obligation is a Lean theorem `soundness : forall env, constraints_hold env -> spec env` -- unconditional, over ALL witnesses, with no random oracle and no computational assumption. So EVERY published protocol that gets its efficiency from a verifier challenge is unavailable to us in its published form, and the failure is not subtle. Worked out on Wesolowski's proof of exponentiation, whose check is pi^l * g^r = y with l the challenge and r = 2^t mod l public: with l fixed at compile time the prover picks ANY pi and outputs y := pi^l * g^r, which verifies by construction at zero work. Because gcd(l, |G|) = 1 makes pi |-> pi^l g^r a BIJECTION of G, every y has an accepting proof -- the equation is a DEFINITION of y, not a constraint on it, and the gadget proves nothing. Wesolowski's own soundness reduction is to the adaptive root game (output u, THEN receive l, THEN produce v with v^l = u); fixing l reverses the quantifiers and the game is won by sampling v and setting u := v^l. Pietrzak has the identical disease with fixed round challenges, and his footnote 5 records an attack that works merely from omitting y from the hash. GENERALISATION, AND THIS IS THE TEST TO APPLY: given a proposed 'witness the answer, check a relation at a fixed public point' construction, ask whether the check is SURJECTIVE onto the claimed output as the free witness ranges over its domain. If it is, the construction is vacuous. THE ESCAPE, WHEN IT EXISTS: if the relation is a polynomial identity of degree d in the challenge, checking it at d+1 DISTINCT FIXED points forces the identity itself and no challenge is needed -- this is derandomisation, not Fiat-Shamir, and it is sound unconditionally. That is the only route by which any challenge-based protocol enters this cost model. See the ecip-derandomized lead.

_meta.uncatalogued_techniques:
THREE TECHNIQUES THAT WON RECORDS BEFORE THEY WERE WRITTEN DOWN, found by diffing archived record trees 2026-08-11. Between them they account for ALL 340 points of a -60 and a -280. The lesson is that this ledger tracks leads found by ANALYSIS while the fleet banks reductions nobody has catalogued -- so diff the reference/prev-* archives after every record, not just the leads.
T1 CONSTANT-OPERAND COLLAPSE: if every limb of one operand of an interpolated multiply is degree 0, the convolution is affine and the entire <2m-1, 2m-1> witness-and-pin step is deleted. Entry condition is `forall j, degree(b[j]) = 0`, NOT AffineW. See vb-const-operand-collapse.
T3 THE VESTIGIAL ALLOCATION: a gadget that stops constraining its top lane still ALLOCATES it, to keep every downstream offset and localLength lemma working -- and that cell is unconstrained, unread, and CHARGED. It hides because the gadget's own docstring says the allocation is deliberate. THE AUDIT: for every gadget compare `witnessVector n` against the range of the forEach that constrains it and against what the return value reads; any index in neither is free. Cost of collecting it is re-deriving every consumer offset.
T4 THE OFFSET-STABILITY TAX: when a gadget's localLength shrinks, a consumer can re-derive its offsets or swap in a costlier gadget of the OLD length. The second is invisible in a diff -- it looks like a gadget choice, not a cost decision. RULE: whenever a diff both shrinks a constant and swaps a gadget elsewhere, the swap is a deferred debt; record it at the size of the debt or it is never collected. See sha-offset-stability-debt.

leads.summary: BANKED, -72 ON VARIABLE BASE, AND THE MECHANISM GENERALISES. Widen a mux's selector to the SUM of two mutually-exclusive flags and pick the ifTrue lane so the second branch produces the CANONICAL value for free — which deletes a whole downstream canonicalisation mux. Nine <4,4> muxes went away at zero cost.
leads.note:
*** THIS WAS FOUND BY THE FLEET, NOT BY THE LEDGER — CATALOGUING IT SO IT TRANSFERS. *** The old row was a plain mux `{ selector := Q.isInf, ifTrue := P.x, ifFalse := x3 }`. The new one keeps ONE mux but changes both the selector and the true-lane: the selector becomes `Q.isInf + cancel`, which is boolean because the two flags are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, and the true-lane becomes the RAW LIMBWISE DIFFERENCE P.x - Q.x, which is a FREE affine form.

WHY BOTH BRANCHES COME OUT RIGHT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE TRICK. On the Q = infinity branch, Q.x is the canonical zero, so the lane evaluates to P.x — exactly the old behaviour. On the CANCELLATION branch, sameX = 1 forces the two canonical x-limb vectors to be equal, so the lane evaluates to the ZERO VECTOR and the output x-coordinate is canonically zero FOR FREE. The second branch therefore no longer needs its own canonicalisation, and the nine-fold canonicalisation mux the GLV table build used to pay for is deleted outright: nine Mux subcircuits (t5x, t6x, t7x, t9x, t10x, t11x and siblings) at <4,4> each = <36,36> = 72, which is exactly the saving. glvBuildTableCost went <14843,14951> -> <14807,14915>.

*** THE GENERAL SHAPE, WHICH IS WHAT TO LOOK FOR ELSEWHERE. *** Wherever two exceptional flags are mutually exclusive, their SUM is boolean at zero cost, so they can share one selector instead of two. Then choose the true-lane as a free affine expression that HAPPENS to collapse to the canonical value on the second flag's branch — a difference rather than a value is the natural candidate, because equality of the two operands makes it vanish. The payoff is not the merged selector itself but the DOWNSTREAM canonicalisation you stop needing.

GREP SIGNATURE: any `Mux` whose ifTrue is a bare variable rather than an expression, sitting upstream of a separate mux or canonicalisation whose only job is to force a canonical zero on some exceptional branch. Look especially in table builds, where the same canonicalisation is repeated once per entry — that repetition is what turned one insight into nine deletions here.

leads.summary: AN ARBITRARY FUNCTION {0,1}^3 -> F_p IS PINNED BY ONE ROW AND ONE ALLOCATION — not just the 192 boolean ones. So ANY number of output bits depending on the same 3 input bits, packed at ANY downstream weights, costs <1,1> IN TOTAL. That is an 8-entry lookup table on 3 existing bits at <1,1>, and a 3:2 compressor at arbitrary output weights at <1,1>.
leads.note:
VERIFIED: 3000/3000 random F: {0,1}^3 -> F_r; 2980/3000 random 3-bit S-box tables; 1968/2000 random BIJECTIVE 3-bit S-boxes. Explicit rows checked over BN254 r for an 8-entry table of random 254-bit field elements, for the S-box [5,2,7,0,3,6,1,4], and for chi + 2*maj. CIRCONOMICON I.1 is the k=1 corner of this.

*** THE NORMAL FORM, PROVED, AND IT SHOWS I.1'S SHAPE IS FORCED RATHER THAN CHOSEN. *** Write a row as (alpha z + A0)(beta z + B0) = gamma z + C0. If alpha*beta != 0 the row is quadratic in z (the I.4 decoy regime). Otherwise wlog beta = 0 and there are exactly two disjoint cases. TYPE 1 (alpha != 0): (z + L2) M = L1 with M affine and non-vanishing on the cube — this IS I.1. TYPE 0 (alpha = 0): z = A0 B0 + affine, requiring multilinear degree <= 2; it is NOT reachable from the Type-1 form and it is how I.2's own twin-packing row works. *** ANY SEARCH THAT ONLY TRIES I.1'S SHAPE SILENTLY MISSES TYPE 0 — at arity 4 that miss is exactly 24 functions. ***

A LINEAR-TIME SOLVABILITY CRITERION (proved, and it is what made every census below tractable): for every U with |U| >= 3, c_U * M(1_U) + sum_{j in U} m_j c_{U\{j}} = 0, where M(1_U) = m_0 + sum_{j in U} m_j. These are LINEAR IN m, because L2*M has degree <= 2 and cannot touch |U| >= 3. So the search is one linear system for the m-space then a linear solve per candidate M — no Groebner basis, no SMT. Corollary used repeatedly: pinnability is CLOSED UNDER RESTRICTION.

*** THE ARITY LADDER, AND THE WALL AT 4 IS SHARP. *** Arity 2: 16/16, proved. Arity 3: 192/256 boolean (184 Type-1 + 8 affine), independently reproducing the tree's SMT number, and GENERICALLY ALL F_p-valued targets. Arity 4: 710/65536, exhaustive over all 222 NPN classes — all 212 degree-2 functions are one-row, degree-3 ones are one-row IFF they have <= 3 essential variables with a pinnable core, and NO DEGREE-4 FUNCTION AT ALL. Arity 5: 0/4000. So A GENUINELY 4-VARIABLE FUNCTION IS ONE-ROW IFF ITS MULTILINEAR DEGREE IS 2. Consequences: chi XOR d, Ch XOR d, XOR4, Maj4 and chi(a XOR d, b, c) are ALL impossible in one row, so THETA'S XOR CANNOT BE FOLDED INTO CHI and chi stays <1,1> per bit. This independently corroborates the exhaustive chi result from the shared-input agent by a completely different route.

A GENUINELY-4-VARIABLE ONE-ROW GADGET EXISTS AND THE SEARCH LESSON MATTERS: F = a + b - ab - ac - bd + cd has all four variables essential and is one-row. Its quadratic support is a 4-CYCLE, and the required rank-2-modulo-diagonal factorisation exists only over a field containing sqrt(-1) — which BN254 has. *** ANY GADGET SEARCH OVER SMALL-INTEGER COEFFICIENTS WILL NEVER FIND THESE; THE COEFFICIENTS ARE 254-BIT. ***

*** DISJOINT PACKING IS SETTLED, WITH PROOFS. *** THEOREM B: Type 1 CANNOT span two disjoint nonlinear blocks. Proof: take S in X1 with |S| = deg f1 and c_S != 0, and any j in X2; applying the criterion to U = S union {j} gives m_j c_S = 0 since F has no cross-block monomials, so m_j = 0, and symmetrically all of X1 — hence M is constant, contradicting Type 1. Confirmed numerically: CHI+lambda CHI, XOR3+lambda XOR3, MAJ3+lambda MAJ3, CH+lambda MAJ3 on disjoint triples all return an EMPTY m-space. TYPE 0 across disjoint blocks: at most TWO, and only difference-of-squares — the reduced coefficients q_ij = alpha_i beta_j + alpha_j beta_i force beta = t alpha on each block with t2 = -t1, i.e. exactly X^2 - Y^2, and three blocks force t = 0. Within a block the pattern forces THE QUADRATIC SUPPORT GRAPH TO BE A CLIQUE. So the tree's empirical 'two per row' now has a proof and a classification.

TWO ACTIONABLE CONSEQUENCES OF THE CLIQUE CRITERION. (1) ALL 16 TWO-VARIABLE GATES ARE SQUARE-TYPE, so ANY TWO 2-INPUT GATES ON DISJOINT INPUTS PACK INTO <1,1> TOTAL — score 1 per gate, verified for all 9x9 nontrivial pairs at lambda in {1,2,4}. This generalises I.3's difference-of-squares from XOR-only to the WHOLE 2-input gate library: (X+Y)(X-Y) = z + L with X = a + (q1/2)b, Y = c - (lambda q2/2)d. (2) Ch IS NOT SQUARE-TYPE — its support is a path, so alpha_f alpha_g = 0 contradicts — hence TWO Ch's ON DISJOINT INPUTS NEED 2 ROWS. Of the 62 degree-2 functions on 3 variables, 38 are square-type.

SAME-INPUT PACKING IS WHERE THE 2x ACTUALLY IS. Over all 256x256 ordered pairs, z = f1 + lambda f2 is one-row for 55,992 pairs at lambda=1, 62,880 at lambda=2 and 63,936 at lambda=4 — i.e. only 2.3%% fail at lambda=4. Verified instances: a 3:2 compressor at weights (1,4) is <1,1> (at (1,2) it is affine and free — the known CSA identity; THE NEW PART IS THAT EVERY OTHER WEIGHT RATIO ALSO COSTS ONLY ONE ROW, so a compressor whose outputs enter a sum at non-adjacent positions is still <1,1>); z = chi(a,b,c) + 2 maj(a,b,c) is <1,1>, two DIFFERENT degree-3 gadgets on the same inputs in one row.

*** THE TABLE RESULT, AND ITS EXACT CROSSOVER AGAINST THE sqrt(N) LAW. *** A 16-entry table on 4 bits is T = T0 + b3(T1 - T0) = <3,3> = score 6, against 19 from I.11's schedule at N=16. Recursing gives 2^{k-2} - 1 rows for N = 2^k. THIS BEATS THE sqrt(N) LAW UP TO ABOUT N = 64, WHERE THEY CROSS — so it does NOT help the fixed-base w=12 selector (N = 2048 would need 511 rows against the peel's 225), but it is the right tool for every SMALL table in the trees.

leads.summary: CARRY THE ACCUMULATOR x AS AN UNREDUCED ALTERNATING SUM OF RAW lambda^2 CONVOLUTIONS FOR THE WHOLE 21-STEP CHAIN, SO IT IS NEVER MATERIALISED. One materialisation plus one degree-3 two-convolution certificate per step instead of two of each. Algebra VERIFIED NUMERICALLY on real secp256k1 points, 0 violations, 21 terms deep. Estimated -6,000 to -11,000.
leads.source: research agent `fixed-base comb and one-hot theory`, 2026-08-12
leads.note:
*** WHERE THE SCORE ACTUALLY IS, FROM THE RECORD'S OWN LEAN COST PROOFS. *** Select12 is <225,225> x 21 = 9,450 (19.9%); ChainExtFold is <855,859> x 19 = 32,566. INSIDE a chain step, 638 of the 855 allocations are range/canonicity bits: stageX <423,425> = <4,0> limbs + <252,256> canonicity + <4,4> convolution + <66,67> quotient range + <97,98> grouped carry fold. Over 21 steps x 2 stages that is ~13,400 allocations of pure bit-pinning, ~26,900 score, 57% OF THE ENTIRE CIRCUIT. THE ACTUAL MULTIPLICATIONS COST 4 ROWS EACH. Lever ranking: (1) materialised 256-bit elements per addition, 57%; (2) grouped carry folds ~17%; (3) THE SELECTOR IS ONLY THIRD at 19.9%.

THE RECURSION, re-derived and verified on real points (50 random scalars, all 21 steps, 0 violations): R2: lambda_i^2 = x_{i+1} + x_i + x_{T_i}; R1: lambda_{i+1}(x_{T_{i+1}} - x_{i+1}) + lambda_i(x_{T_i} - x_{i+1}) = y_{T_{i+1}} + y_{T_i}, all x_T,y_T free affine. y is eliminated entirely — that is why (x, lambda) is the right state. R1 has 2 products, R2 has 1, matching stageC1 + stageX exactly.

*** THE PROPOSAL: UNROLL R2 ALL THE WAY. *** x_{i+1} = sum_{j<=i} (-1)^{i-j} lambda_j^2 - sum_{j<=i} (-1)^{i-j} x_{T_j} + (-1)^{i+1} x_0. VERIFIED NUMERICALLY, 0 violations, 21 terms deep: every accumulator x is an ALTERNATING SUM OF RAW lambda_j^2 CONVOLUTIONS plus free table reads. Two facts make it work: the CELL COUNT DOES NOT GROW (summing 21 convolutions coefficient-wise still leaves 2k-1 cells) and the COEFFICIENTS GROW BY AT MOST 21x, i.e. +5 bits. So x is carried unreduced for the ENTIRE chain and never materialised; only the lambda_i are. Each step then has ONE certificate, R1, degree 3, with TWO CONVOLUTIONS UNDER ONE QUOTIENT.

COST. Current step = 2 x [materialise 512 + cert(D=2) ~343] = 1,714. Proposed = 512 + cert(D=3, two convolutions). BREAK-EVEN IS CERT < 1,202. II.14 prices D=2 at 214, D=3 at 454, D=4 at 1,004 at 8x32. At CERT ~750 and m raised 7 -> 11 (8x32 doubles x_T's operand functionals, selector 450 -> 570 per window) the total is 41,342 (-6,072); at CERT 500 it is 36,092 (-11,322); at CERT 1,000 only -822.

*** PRECONDITION, AND IT IS HARD: THIS NEEDS 8x32 LIMBS. *** II.14 says D=3 is DEAD at 4x64 because the folded position exceeds 2^253. An independent interpolation bound agrees: at 4x64 the carried x polynomial has 7 cells of magnitude <= 4*2^128*21 = 2^134.4 and |lambda(t)||x(t)| at t <= 10 is ~2^233 — under 2^254 but with only ~20 bits of margin BEFORE the second convolution and the quotient term, which is almost certainly the recorded overflow. At 8x32 the same computation gives ~2^204, comfortable. DO THE BOUND ARITHMETIC FIRST.

THE FLOOR THAT SAYS THIS IS THE RIGHT TARGET: a point is determined by x plus one sign bit, 257 bits, not 512. The chain spends 512 bits of advice per step for 257 bits of information. This reaches 256 plus the certificate. That IS the floor.

leads.summary: THE 2*sqrt(mN) SELECTOR LAW MAY NOT BE OPTIMAL AND THE GAP LOOKS LIKE A FACTOR OF 2. Parameter counting says ~110 rows should suffice where the record spends 225, and reachability was verified by exact Gauss-Newton hits at small w. THE BLOCKER IS THE F_p PARAMETER SOLVE, NOT THE LEAN PROOF.
leads.source: research agent `fixed-base comb and one-hot theory`, 2026-08-12
leads.note:
PROVED FIRST, AND IT CONFIRMS THE RECORD. A FULL one-hot of length 2^w costs exactly 2^w - w - 1: all 2^w entries must be affine forms over a witness of dimension w + M + 1 and the minterms are linearly independent, so 2^w <= w + M + 1 (this survives nondeterminism); the split-on-top-bit recursion attains it. For m FUNCTIONALS, PEELING one bit costs exactly m rows and doubles m: R(w,m) = min_j [ m(2^j - 1) + (2^{w-j} - (w-j) - 1) ] ~ 2*sqrt(m 2^w). CALIBRATION: R(11,7) = 105 + 120 = 225, EXACTLY the record's Select12, at split j=4 — the known 2^7 x 2^4 factorisation at m=7. Peeling bit by bit beats materialise-then-contract by 2^j - j - 1.

*** THIS CHALLENGES CIRCONOMICON I.11 ('the sqrt(N) law is within ~3.5x of optimal, stop there'). THAT ADVICE MAY NOT BE SAFE. *** A straight-line circuit with M rows has P(M) = sum_{k=1..M} 2(w+k) + m(w+M+1) parameters against a target of dimension m*2^w, so M >~ sqrt(m 2^w) — A FACTOR 2 BELOW PEEL. At (11,7): peel 225, bound 106. VERIFIED TWO WAYS. (A) Jacobian rank at a random F_p point gives the smallest M with full image dimension: w=4,m=1 needs 2 (peel 4); w=5,m=1 needs 3 (peel 7); w=6,m=1 needs 5 (peel 11); w=6,m=3 needs 9 (peel 20) — tight to 1-2 rows, peel consistently ~2.1x above. (B) Full dimension only shows the target is in the CLOSURE, so damped Gauss-Newton over R was run against RANDOM targets: EXACT HITS to machine precision (~1e-13) at (4,1,2), (4,2,3), (5,1,3), (5,2,4), (6,1,5). Genuinely locally surjective, not merely dominant.

STATUS: CONJECTURE, STRONGLY SUPPORTED NUMERICALLY. If it holds at (11,7), 105-140 rows replace 225: 21 x 115 x 2 = ~4,800, about 10% of the circuit.

*** THE BLOCKER IS THE F_p SOLVE. *** At w=11,m=7 that is 14,336 polynomial equations in ~14,300 unknowns. Gauss-Newton works over R but R-solutions do not transfer to F_p and Newton has no meaning there. NO METHOD IS KNOWN AT THIS SCALE — attack it. Untried: Hensel-lift from a solution mod a small prime; force the first j rows to be the peel and optimise only the tail so the residual system is triangular; the fiber has dimension ~300, so search a rational slice. F_p-rationality is likely by Lang-Weil IF the fiber is geometrically irreducible — not checked. *** THE LEAN BURDEN IS LOW, WHICH IS THE ENCOURAGING PART: *** a deterministic straight-line construction makes each row a DEFINITION z_k := A_k * B_k, so soundness and completeness are automatic and correctness is a FINITE IDENTITY OVER 2048 POINTS.

*** DO NOT ATTACK IT WITH TENSOR RANK, PENCILS OR SIMULTANEOUS DIAGONALISATION — THREE INDEPENDENT REASONS. *** (a) The classical bilinear methods are ALREADY WORSE than trivial contraction: at K=16,L=128,m=7 the flattening lower bound on bilinear rank is min(128,112) = 112 products while naive contraction is m(K-1) = 105 — naive BEATS the bilinear bound because it uses sum_a e_a = 1, a ONE-HOT relation not a bilinear identity, so general linear-form decompositions are a priori handicapped. (b) Simultaneous diagonalisation needs the pencil's characteristic polynomial to split over F_p: probability ~1/n! for generic limbs. (c) Even at the best tensor rank the dimension bound mKL/(K+L+m-2) = 96 against 105 is a <=4% win, and at the OPTIMAL split the two coincide asymptotically. THE FACTOR OF 2 MUST COME FROM BREAKING THE FACTORISATION, NOT FROM A BETTER CONTRACTION.

ALSO NEGATIVE: fusing selector with multiplication (the peel's payload must be affine in the INNER one-hot at every level, and III.5's 'payload is free' IS the statement that it is compile-time constant; it survives only at the final contraction, which is the product you already had). AND the POWER BASIS is an exact substitute for the one-hot, worse by v-1, with Paterson-Stockmeyer reproducing the same 2*sqrt(mN) — so this factor-2 gap IS the long-standing sqrt(n) vs 2*sqrt(n) gap in preconditioned polynomial evaluation.

leads.summary: THE ONLY PLACE IN THE RSA CHALLENGE WHERE THE CLASSICAL MULTIPLICATION LOWER BOUNDS DO NOT BIND. WindowSquare beats the Fiduccia-Zalcstein 2m-1 count by ~2x, but the record applies it ONLY to squares. Generalising it to the general bilinear case should pay on the ternary step. PARKED: rsa has no slots in tick.py SLOTS.
leads.note:
*** WHY THE LOWER BOUND DOES NOT APPLY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. *** Fiduccia-Zalcstein prices COMPUTING ALL 2m-1 CONVOLUTION COEFFICIENTS. The circuit does not need them: the grouped carry check reads only the 2K group sums S_w = sum_{i<g} coeff(gw+i) 2^{Bi}. Pinning 2K ~ 38 field elements is a STRICTLY WEAKER obligation than pinning 341 coefficients, and the theorem says nothing about it. This is the single exception in the problem and it is already worth 4,528 in the shipped record (326,297 analysed minus 321,769 shipped, against a predicted 304 per squaring x 15 = 4,560 — it accounts for the delta essentially exactly).

THE MECHANISM. Write a = sum B_u Z^u with Z = X^9. For a scalar point c put G_c(X) = sum B_u(X) c^u. Splitting G_c^2 into low (0..8) and high (9..16): Lo(c) + t^9 Hi(c) = G_c(t)^2 = beta(c)^2 with beta affine — ONE product; and t^9 Hi(c) = sum_{i+j>=9} h_i h_j, a RANK-8 QUADRATIC FORM WHICH FACTORS INTO FOUR PRODUCTS by the hyperbolic-pairing rule (ceil(r/2) rows for a rank-r form). Total 5 rows and 4 allocations per point plus the 2K cells: 10K allocations and 10K rows against 2(2m-1) = 36K for coefficient-wise interpolation. General form: score = 4K(h+1) with h = ceil((g-1)/2), i.e. ~2m + 4m/g against ~4m.

*** THE LEAD: THE RECORD USES THIS ONLY FOR SQUARES. *** The construction needs G_c^2 — a SQUARE — to make the low/high split a single product. For a general multiply G_c * H_c the analogue is Lo + t^9 Hi = beta(c) gamma(c), still ONE product, but t^9 Hi = sum_{i+j>=9} g_i h_j is now a BILINEAR form of rank 8 rather than a QUADRATIC form of rank 8 — and a rank-r bilinear form costs r rows, not ceil(r/2), because the hyperbolic pairing needs the symmetry. So 1 + 8 = 9 rows per point instead of 5, giving 18K rows — still well below 36K. It should therefore pay for the ternary step and for any non-square multiply, at roughly 2m instead of 4m. The ternary step costs 34,165 with overhead 9,592 and does not appear to use it; estimate ~1,000-2,000.

*** FIRST THING TO CHECK, AND IT IS EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED: the rank of the general bilinear Hi form. *** The rank-8 figure is inferred from the square case, not proved. If it is higher than 8 the saving shrinks or vanishes. Establish the rank before doing any of the algebra.

leads.summary: SIX CLOSED DIRECTIONS ON RSA, ALL FLOWING FROM ONE PROVEN INVARIANT: score = 2 x (total advice bits), INDEPENDENT OF LIMB WIDTH. That is why Barrett, Montgomery and every re-limbing are bit-identical, and why 80.3% of the record is range checks that are irreducible for this reduction scheme.
leads.note:
(1) BARRETT IS BIT-IDENTICAL TO PLAIN. Multiplying by the precomputed mu is FREE (affine), but each floor division needs the discarded low part witnessed and range-checked: 8,190 for the first floor plus 8,192 for the final t, total 16,382. The 'cheap constant multiply' that makes Barrett attractive in software IS the part that was already free.

(2) MONTGOMERY IS A PURE LOSS OF ~10%. Per step it is also 16,384 — witness m' and res, both 4096 bits, with division by R = 2^4096 free as limb re-indexing. But domain entry and exit each cost a full extra reduction (+16,382 each), so 17 steps plus 2 conversions is +32,764 on the challenge. For contrast circom-rsa-verify uses Montgomery CIOS and reports 536,212 constraints + 530,676 wires for RSA-2048 — ~3.3x our record at HALF the modulus size, about 13x per bit.

(3) RNS IS 59x TO 215x WORSE. A 'small modular multiplication mod m_i' is not free in F_r: it costs 4w+1. RNS Montgomery needs ~2n(n+1) of them per reduction for the two base extensions, which Bajard-Didier-Kornerup themselves call 'the bottlenecks of the method'. At w=32,n=128 that is 4,309,632 against 20,004. THE EXCHANGE RATE IS BACKWARDS: RNS spends O(n^2) modular reductions to save O(n^2) linear recombinations, and linear recombination costs ZERO here. NOTE THE DEEPER POINT — our evaluation-point technique ALREADY IS a CRT/RNS, with moduli (X - rho_i) whose reduction is evaluation, hence affine, hence free. RNS is already deployed in the only version that pays.

(4) NOTHING BEATS TOOM-COOK FULL-WIDTH, AND MINIMISING THE MULTIPLY IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL. Fiduccia-Zalcstein gives rank exactly 2m-1 over a large-enough field (condition 2m-1 <= r+1, non-binding for any m <= 2^253), and recursive Karatsuba is a WORSE INSTANCE OF THE SAME FAMILY (3^7 = 2,187 against 2*128-1 = 255). NTT ties at best: the transforms are constant linear maps hence free, so an NTT costs exactly its length, and length >= 2m-1 is forced for a linear convolution — at length 2m-1 the NTT LITERALLY IS the evaluation scheme with roots of unity as points. The floor is 67 rows at B=122, m=34 — but B=122 forces carry-group width 1 and the carry chain explodes to 17,094 overhead against 2,859 at the record's B=24. The multiplication is ~0.3% of the cost and is NOT the binding constraint; the record's machine-checked LimbWidth optimum (24, flat basin 15-27) is correct and my model's preference for B=12 is ~10% optimistic — TRUST THE RECORD'S TABLES.

(5) SQUARING HAS NO COEFFICIENT-LEVEL SAVING, AND THIS IS PROVED. The 2m-1 coefficients of A(X)^2 are LINEARLY INDEPENDENT QUADRATIC FORMS in the a_i; each R1CS row supplies one rank-1 quadratic form, so >= 2m-1 rows, identical to a general multiply. The m(m+1)/2 vs m^2 'distinct products' is SCHOOLBOOK accounting that evaluation/interpolation already ignores — A(rho)A(rho) is one product exactly as A(rho)B(rho) is. Bounds do not improve either. The saving is at the GROUP-SUM level only (see rsa-windowsquare-bilinear).

(6) THE DEGREE LADDER IS WORTH EXACTLY ZERO ON RSA, AND THIS IS THE CLEANEST EXPLANATION OF WHY THE TWO CHALLENGES DIVERGE. Merging into a degree-D certificate: residue k bits, quotient (D-1)k bits, total Dk bits for log2(D) squarings, so D=2 and D=4 TIE EXACTLY at 2k per squaring and D>=8 loses (2.67k, then 4k). At D=4 the overhead is strictly worse, so D=2 wins. The quotient advice grows in LOCKSTEP with the residue advice you save. On secp256k1 the pseudo-Mersenne fold collapses the quotient to a single ~38-bit wire, so raising D costs nothing on the quotient side — which is why the same technique is worth -29,200 there.

(7) TWO MORE, BRIEFLY. Deferred accumulation has a budget of log2 M <= 252 - 2B - log2 m, i.e. 2^196 at the record's parameters — IT NEVER BINDS, so 'choose the limb width to maximise deferred reduction' has no content; the width is set entirely by the cells-versus-carries trade. And MODULUS SCALING is dead twice over: finding k with kN = 2^L - rho and rho small needs a ~2^4032 search, while a sparse multiple doubles the operands to 8,192 bits so the residue advice goes 8,192 -> 16,384, EXACTLY CANCELLING the quotient you deleted — zero gain even with a free oracle for k.

leads.summary: A THIRD DERANDOMISATION FOR MULTISET EQUALITY, WITH A DIFFERENT ASYMPTOTIC: Theta(n log K) instead of Theta(n log n), where K is the size of the value domain. Beats Waksman and the product tree whenever K < n and the elements ALREADY ARRIVE BIT-DECOMPOSED. No prior art found.
leads.note:
WHY THIS IS WORTH READING: two independent constructions (Waksman, derandomised product tree) both land near 2n log2 n, and that agreement was being read as evidence that 2n log2 n IS the price of a challenge-free multiset argument. IT IS NOT, when the value domain is small.

THE CONSTRUCTION. Elements a_i in [0,K) with K = 2^k, given by their ALREADY-BOOLEAN bits b_{i,j}. Fix a compile-time base X = n+1 and define H(a) = sum_i X^{a_i}, where X^{a_i} = prod_{j=0}^{k-1} (1 + b_{i,j} (X^{2^j} - 1)). Each factor is a FREE AFFINE FORM because the X^{2^j} are compile-time constants, so the product costs k-1 rows and k-1 allocations per element. Then assert H(a) = H(b), a free affine equation.

SOUNDNESS, WITH NO CHALLENGE. H(a) = sum_{j<K} c_j X^j with c_j the multiplicity of value j. Since 0 <= c_j <= n < X and n*X^{K-1} < p, the lift of H(a) to the integers IS its base-X representation, which is unique. So H(a) = H(b) implies identical histograms implies multiset equality — for EVERY witness. This is radix separation (Kronecker substitution) applied to multiplicities. SIDE CONDITION: (K-1)*log2(n+1) + log2 n <= 253.

COST: 2n(k-1) - 1 per witnessed side, and ZERO for a side that is a PUBLIC multiset, because its histogram is a compile-time constant. Measured: n=256 K=8, 2,048 both sides against Waksman 3,586 and product tree 3,966; n=1024 K=8, 8,192 against 18,434 and 19,966; n=4096 K=16, 49,152 against 90,114. Crossover is K < n, subject to the capacity bound, which caps K at about 32 for n~256 and 16 for n>=1024.

*** THE CAVEAT THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT APPLIES TO US. *** The bits must ALREADY be boolean in the circuit. If you must decompose first, add 2k-1 per element and the method LOSES to Waksman everywhere (n=1024, K=16: 26,624 against 18,434). So this is for circuits where small-domain values already arrive bit-decomposed — hash byte and nibble lanes, digit decompositions, one-hot-adjacent data. Check that precondition before pricing anything.

leads.summary: A SEARCH DIRECTIVE, NOT A GADGET. For a genus-0 (rational) variety, certifying membership costs the monomials of the PARAMETRISATION, not the degree of the implicit equation: a degree-d rational curve costs ceil(log2 d) rows rather than d. Sweep the gadget library for varieties being implicitised by reflex.
leads.note:
THE EXAMPLE THAT MAKES IT CONCRETE. A point on the unit circle: implicit x^2 + y^2 = 1 is <1,2> = 3. The homogeneous rational parametrisation (X,Y,Z) = (1 - t^2, 2t, 1 + t^2) needs ONE row u = t*t and everything else is free affine — score 2. The prover witnesses the PARAMETER and the circuit checks the parametrisation, instead of witnessing the point and checking the implicit equation.

*** IT ALSO EXPLAINS, IN ONE SENTENCE, WHY THE ELLIPTIC-CURVE CHALLENGES COST WHAT THEY COST. *** Genus 1 admits NO rational parametrisation, so there is no parametric shortcut and the group law is the only structure available. Carry that alongside the Semaev and elliptic-net negatives.

vb-lambda-elim is one instance of this found by hand. The directive is to look for others systematically: anywhere we assert an implicit polynomial relation on a witnessed point, ask whether the variety is rational and whether witnessing a parameter is cheaper.

leads.summary: 17 MODULAR MULTIPLICATIONS IS A PROVED FLOOR FOR a^65537, NOT MERELY THE BEST KNOWN CHAIN — AND THERE IS ZERO SLACK. The exponentiation structure is closed; the only lever is per-modmul cost, which is ~99% range checks. Every sublinear proof-of-exponentiation is both unsound here AND slower than 17.
leads.note:
UPPER BOUND: the addition-chain length of 65537 is exactly 17, since each step at most doubles the maximum, so after k steps max <= 2^k and 65537 > 2^16. LOWER BOUND, THE NEW PART: take N prime for the argument; the graph {(a, a^e)} in F_N^2 is a curve of degree e = 65537, any R1CS with k rows cuts a variety of degree <= 2^k, and Bezout survives linear projection, so the projection to (a,c) has degree <= 2^k, giving k >= ceil(log2 65537) = 17. NOTE HOW TIGHT: ceil(log2 65537) = addition-chain-length(65537) = 17 EXACTLY, because 65537 is one more than a power of two. For a generic 17-bit exponent there would be a gap worth attacking; here there is none. SCOPE CAVEAT, STATED HONESTLY: this bounds programs expressible as ring operations in Z/N, and our circuit is over F_r simulating Z/N, so it transfers as '>= 17 modmuls' rather than '>= 17 rows'.

*** EVERY SUBLINEAR PoE DIES TWICE. *** Wesolowski: the verifier sends a RANDOM PRIME l, and Boneh-Bunz-Fisch note the advantage is always at least 1/|Primes(lambda)| because an adversary guessing l outputs w = u^l. With l fixed and public that guess is FREE: pick u != 1, set w := u^l, claim h' := h*w, send pi := u*g^q — accepted, zero work. Pietrzak: with r fixed the prover picks alpha != 1 and DEFINES the low-order element as alpha^(2^{T/2} - r). Bellare-Garay-Rabin batch verification is probabilistic and amortises over MANY exponentiations. AND THEY LOSE EVEN IF SOUND: at T=16 Wesolowski's verifier is two 256-bit exponentiations, about 500-770 modmuls, Pietrzak about 1,900-2,500 — against 17. Crossover is around T ~ 512 squarings. CLOSE THIS DIRECTION PERMANENTLY.

WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS: about 5.2 constraints per bit of modulus per modmul, derived by hand from zk-email's FpMul circom source — 2(2k-1) limb products, then 2kn bits of quotient/remainder range checks plus carry and comparison. Range checks are ~99% of it. Fusing reductions and dropping FULL reduction on the 16 intermediate squarings is the right shape; zk-email already skips it on the last because the padded message is necessarily smaller than the modulus.

leads.summary: TWO LOWER BOUNDS AND ONE IMPOSSIBILITY, ALL CLOSING SEARCHES. n independent booleans need >= n rows (Krull height). A k-bit digit check needs >= k rows (degree doubling). And AGGREGATED booleanity — one row proving many bits boolean — is not merely unsound, it is NOT EXPRESSIBLE as a single R1CS row for any n >= 2.
leads.note:
*** (1) n BOOLEANS NEED n ROWS, WHATEVER YOU DO. *** Let V be the solution set of k rows in n bit-variables plus m auxiliary witnesses, with all 2^n patterns reachable. By Krull's height theorem every component of V has dimension >= n+m-k; each component projects into the finite set {0,1}^n hence into a single point, so has dimension <= m. Therefore k >= n. This holds for ANY polynomial constraint system and REGARDLESS OF HOW MANY AUXILIARY WITNESSES you add. So the only lever is amortisation — making a row you needed anyway also pin booleanity — which we already do.

*** (2) AGGREGATED BOOLEANITY IS INEXPRESSIBLE, NOT JUST UNSOUND. *** sum_i b_i(1-b_i) has quadratic part with Gram matrix -I of rank n, while a product of two affine forms has quadratic part of rank <= 2. So for n >= 3 it is immediately not rank-1. For n = 2 the rank test PASSES (over BN254-Fr, -1 is a QR so b1^2+b2^2 factors), and the full factorisation was checked by hand: b1+b2-b1^2-b2^2 = -(s-b)(t-a) - ab with a = 1/2 - i/2, b = 1/2 + i/2, and a single row needs the residual ab = 0, but ab != 0 over BN254-Fr. So EVEN TWO variables cannot be aggregated into one row. It would also be unsound: an explicit BN254 pair with b1(1-b1) + b2(1-b2) = 0 and neither b_i in {0,1} was produced — the conic has ~p points, so cancellation is generic, not exotic.

*** (3) SUM-OF-SQUARES: THE TWO CONDITIONS ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. *** Over any finite field every element is a sum of two squares, so with >= 3 terms sum x_i^2 = 0 ALWAYS has a nontrivial zero (write -1 = a^2+b^2, take (a,b,1)). With 2 terms it is sound iff -1 is a non-residue, i.e. q = 3 mod 4 — and BN254-Fr and BLS12-381-Fr are both 1 mod 4, so it fails outright for us. Worse, in exactly the sound case (q = 3 mod 4) the form does NOT factor into two affine forms, so it is not a legal row. Soundness and rank-1 expressibility cannot both hold. The Bulletproofs-style aggregation that DOES work needs a VERIFIER CHALLENGE (Bunz et al. §4.1: 'take a random linear combination chosen by the verifier'), which plain R1CS does not have — hard-coding one lets the prover choose the witness after seeing the constant, and the n/p bound evaporates. Same fixed-challenge rule as _meta.fixed_challenge_rule.

*** (4) HIGHER-RADIX DIGIT CHECKS SAVE EXACTLY 1, ONCE, AND DO NOT SCALE. *** A k-bit digit can be pinned in k rows + (k-1) auxiliary witnesses = 2k-1, against 2k for k separate bits. Verified for k=2 (u=x, w=x^2, then (w-3x)(w-3x+2)=0, brute-forced to exactly {0,1,2,3}) and k=3 (centre u = x - 7/2, w = u^2, t = w^2, then one quadratic-in-t row, brute-forced to exactly {0..7}). The saving is 1 INDEPENDENT OF k. And k rows is OPTIMAL: after m rows every witness is a polynomial in x of degree <= 2^m, while the final row must vanish exactly on a set of size 2^k so has degree >= 2^k, giving m >= k. CONSEQUENCE — DO NOT BUILD A BASE-2^k DECOMPOSITION: n bits as d = n/k digits costs d digit-witnesses + d*k rows + d*(k-1) aux = 2n, IDENTICAL to plain bits. It only wins at d = 1, i.e. the whole value as one digit, for 2n-1 — which is exactly what our RangeCheck.main already achieves by witnessing n-1 bits and deriving the top affinely. NO SAVING AVAILABLE. This independently reproduces the `rangefloor` job's 2n-1 by a completely different argument.

*** (5) HYGIENE, AND IT IS THE STANDARD BUG CLASS. *** The free-output-booleanity trick (a row linear in the output whose leading coefficient never vanishes on the cube) is EXACTLY as sound as the INPUT booleanity it rests on — the degree collapse a^2 -> a is what makes it work. All three major frontends institutionalise this with named API (arkworks new_witness_without_booleanity_check, gnark MarkBoolean, gnark WithUnconstrainedOutputs), and circomlib's gates.circom does it WITHOUT checking its inputs, which is exploitable by setting one input to the modular inverse of the other. Real instances: Polygon zkEVM's isNeg and rkeyBit missing binary constraints, both attacker-controllable.

*** INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED BY A SECOND AGENT, 2026-08-12, VIA A DIFFERENT ARGUMENT. *** The degree-2 part of any R1CS row is (a.w)(b.w), a rank-<=2 quadratic form that SPLITS OVER F_p BY CONSTRUCTION. Restricted to any two free witness coordinates a row is therefore a plane conic whose quadratic part is a product of two F_p-linear forms, so it always has an F_p point at infinity and is either empty, a line, two lines, a smooth conic with ~p affine points, or the whole plane — NEVER A FINITE NONEMPTY SET OF >= 2 POINTS. Hence one row cannot cut two otherwise-free coordinates to {0,1}^2 and two booleanities cost >= 2 rows. Numerically: b1(b1-1) + b2(b2-1) = 0 has 10,008 solutions mod 10,007, not 4. THE SAME ARGUMENT EXPLAINS WHY THE ANISOTROPIC TRICK FAILS: x^2 - N y^2 = 0 with N a non-residue WOULD collapse two zero-assertions into one row, but an anisotropic binary form is exactly one that does NOT factor into two linear forms, so it cannot be written as an R1CS row at all. That is the assertion-side dual of I.9. A NARROW EXCEPTION worth knowing: if b1,b2 are already known to be non-negative integers < M with 2M^2 < p, then (b1 + i b2)(b1 - i b2) = b1 + b2 with i = sqrt(-1) proves both booleanities in <0,1>, because over the integers each b(b-1) >= 0. The range precondition is NECESSARY, not an artefact — and freshly witnessed advice bits have no prior bound, so this is rarely available.

RADIX RANGE CHECKS INDEPENDENTLY RECONFIRMED AS A TIE, BY EXPLICIT CONSTRUCTION: a base-4 digit via (d)(d-3) = t then (t)(t+2) = 0 accepts exactly {0,1,2,3}, and costs 1 digit alloc + 1 aux alloc + 2 constraints = 4 per 2 bits against binary's 4. Base 8 is 6 per 3 bits against 6. Base 16 is 10 per 4 bits against 8 — WORSE. The auxiliary allocation eats the constraint saving precisely. Also: one row CANNOT certify a 2-bit digit with no new witness, since two quadratics in d alone have at most 2 common roots.

AND A NOTE ON WHAT LOWER-BOUND THEORY TO SEARCH: our cost measure is the OSTROWSKI MEASURE / NON-SCALAR COMPLEXITY C*, defined in exactly our row form by Brand-Kaski-Wang (arXiv:2607.02241) as f_j = s_j t_j with s_j, t_j in span{1, X_1..X_q, f_1..f_{j-1}}. SEARCH THAT VOCABULARY, NEVER 'multiplicative complexity' ALONE — that term is owned by the GF(2) literature and returns the wrong corpus. Tools that bite: the degree bound deg <= 2^L; dimension/parameter counting (Jarlebring-Lorentzon Thm 4.2, and Giusti-Heintz-Kuijpers eq. 1 for the multi-output version, which is the rigorous ancestor of V.3); the substitution method (BCS Ch. 6); Strassen's degree bound. Tools that DO NOT apply: TENSOR RANK BREAKS PAST BILINEAR — Strassen's L ~ R holds only for 3-tensors, and Brand-Kaski-Wang exhibit a form with L <= 2n+1 but R = n^2, so for our degree-3 multilinear gadgets (Maj, chi), which are 4-tensors, tensor rank is the WRONG TOOL and the gap can be n^2 against 2n+1. Also inapplicable: Raz's multilinear bounds (they bound total size, not multiplication count), border and monotone rank, and every GF(2)/XAG result. Strassen 1973 also settles that DIVISIONS DO NOT HELP in the deterministic model (C* = C*/ over infinite fields) — though our NONDETERMINISTIC witnessed-inverse trick is outside that model and is not covered.

leads.summary: THE ONE STRUCTURAL LEVER LEFT BELOW ~260,000. The fused 2A+T step materialises FIVE 256-bit elements (lambda1, x_S, A, x4, y4) at 512 each. Is there a 2A+T formula needing only FOUR? That is ~44,000 off the variable-base record.
leads.source: research agent `amortized inversion and EC formulas`, 2026-08-12
leads.note:
THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS THE LAST LEVER. In this model one materialised 256-bit F_q element costs 512 (2 per bit) and one degree-2 congruence certificate costs 196, with a full non-native multiply-to-new-element at 717. The variable-base step is measured to sit EXACTLY ON ITS FLOOR at five materialisations: the step floor is ~3,897 (~280,000 overall) against a target that needs 4,212, and the local floor analysis says not one point is recoverable WITHOUT dropping a materialisation. So the question is not 'can this row be shaved' but 'does a 2A+T formula exist with four materialised elements'. Flagged in the corpus as best-known-formula rather than proved, so it is genuinely open.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES IT PLAUSIBLE. The fused Eisentrager-Lauter-Montgomery double-add already removes one materialisation the naive route pays: fusedStepCost <2034,2047> = 4,081 against 5,735 unfused, because the intermediate y NEVER BECOMES A WIRE. That is the same trick applied once. The question is whether it applies twice. Look at the degree ladder (CIRCONOMICON II.14): merging two rows into one degree-3 certificate that never materialises x_R costs 454 against 531 to materialise, a gain of 290 — AT 8x32 LIMBS. At 4x64 the same merge overflows and LOSES 700. So limb width decides whether the technique exists at all; do the bound arithmetic before the algebra.

leads.summary: SIX CLOSED DIRECTIONS ON THE CURVE CHALLENGES, ALL FLOWING FROM ONE FACT: in this model I = M = S = one reduction (717), so every ECC optimisation since 1985 — which exists to trade inversions for multiplications — RUNS BACKWARDS HERE. Do not spend slots on any of these.
leads.source: research agent `amortized inversion and EC formulas`, 2026-08-12
leads.note:
*** THE PREMISE FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE THING TO REMEMBER. *** 'An inversion is one row' is true in the NATIVE field and FALSE in the emulated base field: a hinted inverse still needs certifying by x*inv = 1 mod q, which is a full modular-reduction certificate. So an inversion is 717 — and so is a multiply. I = M = S EXACTLY. The right unit of account is not M/S/I but MATERIALISATIONS: one materialised 256-bit element (512) plus one degree-2 congruence (196) per absorbed point.

(1) MONTGOMERY BATCH INVERSION — NEVER, AT ANY n, IN EITHER REGIME. Batching costs 1 inversion + 3(n-1) multiplies, so it pays iff I > 3M. Here I = M, so the loss is exactly 2(n-1)*717 = 1434(n-1): n=2 loses 1,434, n=8 loses 10,038, n=62 loses 87,474. It is worse in allocations alone too (3n-2 materialisations vs n). Even under the optimistic 'inversion is one row' premise it loses 4(n-1). THE CORRECT VERSION OF THE INSTINCT is LAZY REDUCTION, which amortises the CERTIFICATE (~424 rows) against extra CONVOLUTIONS (~15): measured 424 / 228 / 123 / 69 rows per multiplication at M = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, a 6.1x amortisation, and worth -2,998 where it landed. Grep signature: two or more mod-reduction subcircuits whose outputs feed a common assertion.

(2) PROJECTIVE / JACOBIAN / co-Z / COMPLETE FORMULAS — 2.3x to 5.3x WORSE THAN AFFINE. Priced at 717 per reduction: affine ADD 3 reductions (2,151), Jacobian mmadd 6, co-Z zadd 7, RCB complete ADD 12, Jacobian/projective add-2007-bl 16 (11,472). RCB's multiply-by-3b is free here so its usual advantage evaporates. The deeper reason is ALGEBRAIC DEGREE, not operation counts: an unreduced convolution can serve as a multiplicand only up to degree 2 at 64-bit limbs or 3 at 32-bit, and Jacobian X3 is degree 9 and Y3 degree 13, forcing >= 4 materialisations; affine-with-witnessed-slope is degree 2 and hits 1-3.

(3) x-ONLY / DIFFERENTIAL ADDITION — 2.6x worse AND UNSOUND FOR FIXED BASE. The Brier-Joye a=0 identities (PKC 2002 Prop 2(6),2(7)) are degree 4, verified 200/200 on random secp256k1 points. Per OPERATION it is a wash (1,516 vs 1,434), but it dies structurally: a differential chain must pin x(P-Q), which FORCES A LADDER (512 ops vs the record's 62 steps), which forbids windowing, which forbids the 4-dim fake-GLV MSM that is the whole 3.3x. *** AND IT IS UNSOUND, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE COST. *** Without a pinned difference the chaining relation has BOTH x(P+T) and x(P-T) as roots — verified 0/600 failures on both roots, roots distinct 300/300, root set of +P equal to that of -P 200/200 — so the sign ambiguity cannot cancel globally and a prover gets a free sign per window. y-recovery is NOT the problem (Brier-Joye Prop 3, ~5 reductions once).

(4) wNAF AND JOINT SPARSE FORM ARE WORTH EXACTLY ZERO IN A CIRCUIT, AND THIS GENERALISES. Their entire advantage is AVERAGE-CASE digit sparsity (density 1/(w+1) vs 1/2; Solinas's 1/2 joint density). A circuit is built for the WORST CASE — every position nonzero — so they buy nothing over a fixed window of the same width while adding data-dependent digit logic. IN-CIRCUIT, JSF IS IDENTICAL TO PLAIN INTERLEAVING. Carry the general rule: any technique whose benefit is an AVERAGE over inputs is worth zero here.

(5) ALTERNATIVE CURVE MODELS ARE IMPOSSIBLE, BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES. #E(secp256k1) is prime with cofactor 1, hence odd, so by Lagrange there is no rational point of order 2, 3 or 4. Independently, a Montgomery model needs a root of x^3 + ax + b; for a=0,b=7 that means alpha^3 = -7, and q = 1 mod 3 makes cubing 3-to-1 with (-7)^((q-1)/3) != 1, so x^3+7 has NO ROOT in F_q. Therefore Montgomery, Edwards, twisted Edwards, Jacobi quartic, Huff, Hessian and twisted Hessian are ALL unavailable, and every F_q-isogenous curve shares the order so no model in the isogeny class works either. SHORT WEIERSTRASS AFFINE IS THE ONLY MODEL THIS CURVE ADMITS. Note the pleasing tension: q = 1 mod 3 is simultaneously what forces this and what supplies the GLV endomorphism.

(6) SEMAEV SUMMATION POLYNOMIALS AND DIVISION POLYNOMIALS. S3 IS the x-only relation above (for b=7 it symmetrises to the 9-monomial e2^2 - 4 e1 e3 - 28 e1 = 0); S4 has 191 monomials at degree 12 and S5 is degree 32. psi_n is degree n^2. Dead. Also: deriving y_T from x_T instead of muxing needs a square root at 3 reductions/step against 56 for the whole tree mux — 40x worse.

leads.summary: THE REFUTATION IS REAL BUT DOES NOT TRANSFER TO ANY TARGET WE HAVE. Sharing inputs does break the disjoint-block barrier, but an exhaustive search settled the two places it was aimed: KECCAK CHI IS AT A PROVED FLOOR (10 per 5-bit lane row, zero slack) and SHA-256 Maj does not pack. What survives is an EXACT DECISION PROCEDURE for single-row encodability, and a confirmed win for Ch across adjacent rounds.
leads.note:
*** WHAT IS CLOSED, AND IT IS CLOSED PROPERLY. *** For gadgets on DISJOINT input blocks over a field with 2 != 0: `degree_three_never_packs` (two non-affine gadgets, nonzero multiplier, packed target of multilinear degree >= 3: NO row pins it), `three_gadgets_never_pack` (three gadgets on pairwise disjoint blocks never share a row, whatever their degrees), `and3_never_packs`, `maj_never_packs`, and `degree_two_packs_at_most_two` with the cap ATTAINED by `two_and2_gadgets_pack`. The exhaustive multiplier search and the 759,375-candidate Maj search that both came back empty are now EXPLAINED rather than merely unexplained, so stop re-running them. Note the formalisation is STRONGER than 'no unique determination': `Row.Pins` allows soundness up to one affine DECOY ROOT, and the decoy branch is handled first, so a decoy trick cannot evade the result.

*** WHAT IS OPEN, AND THIS IS THE LEAD. *** `shared_degree_three_packs` REFUTES the same statement for gadgets sharing input variables, with an explicit witness over Q: the row `(1 + x1 + x2) * z = x0` pins z UNIQUELY — no decoy — because `1 + x1 + x2` never vanishes on the cube. The pinned value x0/(1 + x1 + x2) has multilinear form `x0 - x0*x1/2 - x0*x2/2 + x0*x1*x2/3`, genuinely CUBIC (coefficient 1/3 on the top term), and it splits as f + 1*g with f non-affine on one triple and g non-affine on another. `shared_three_degree_two_gadgets_pack` refutes the three-gadget bound the same way. `pinned_target_of_degree_three` pinpoints the exact step that needs disjointness. Also `exists_two_nonaffine_triples_packing`: even on DISJOINT triples two non-affine degree-2 gadgets do share a row, so the degree hypothesis in the negative result cannot be dropped.

*** THE TECHNIQUE, STATED GENERALLY. *** A row L(x)*z = R(x) with L,R affine and L NOWHERE ZERO ON THE BOOLEAN CUBE pins z uniquely to the rational function R/L, and R/L can have HIGHER multilinear degree than any product of affine forms. That is the whole mechanism, and it costs ONE row and ONE allocation. The open question is which multilinear targets are reachable as R/L with L nowhere-vanishing.

Best parametrisation needs 4n+10 FIXED LINES, i.e. 14 for a single-point MSM -- not the 'under 10' hoped for but far under the 49 of the published form. *** VACUITY, SETTLED EMPIRICALLY. *** With A0 fixed at compile time the check is SURJECTIVE onto Q. Concrete forgery: set b=0, a_den=1, a_num=c0+c1*x (inside the allowed degree bounds); the check collapses to ONE linear equation c0*(coeff0-coeff2) + c1*(coeff0*u - coeff2*x2) = rho in two unknowns, so every claimed Q has an accepting witness. Verified: 200/200 random wrong Q forged, zero circuit work. So single-point ECIP is vacuous, not merely unproven. Confirms _meta.fixed_challenge_rule.

*** THE DERANDOMISATION COUNT, DERIVED. *** The identity is a rational function of the challenge; force it by evaluating at deg+1 fixed points. Measured degrees (three parametrisations, all verified numerically against a genuine garaga witness on secp256k1):
  (a) garaga's published TANGENT form (A2 = -2*A0, parametrise by x_A0): needs 20n+29 distinct x-coordinates, each used at both +-v. n=1 -> 49. The blow-up is the composition with [-2], a degree-4 map.
  (b) MY REFORMULATION, pencil of lines through a FIXED auxiliary point A1 (so A2 = -(A0+A1), a degree-1 map): 10n+21. n=1 -> 31. Derived by differentiating Weil reciprocity along that family; verified 10/10 against garaga's honest witness.
  (c) BEST: Eagen's own MIXED form (his eval_function_challenge_mixed) derandomised over the PENCIL OF PARALLEL LINES y = m x + b, m fixed at compile time, b the parameter. The three intersection points are conjugate over F_p(b), so the LHS is a FIELD TRACE and the whole identity is a rational function of the single parameter b. Verified 12/12 on secp256k1 with m fixed. Count: 6n+12 lines. n=1 -> 18.
  (d) (c) PLUS a common-denominator witness encoding: garaga's a_den always DIVIDES b_den (verified 18/18 across n=1,2,4), so witness (a_num deg n+3, b_num deg n+1, D deg n+4) with alpha=a_num/D, beta=b_num/D. Then 4n+10 lines. n=1 -> 14, n=2 -> 18, n=4 -> 26.
EXACT LAW, verified by sweeping each degree independently: deg_b(Phi) = 2*deg(denominator) + (#basis points). NUMERATOR degrees cost NOTHING. So the only lever left is shrinking the denominator.

*** THE COST MODEL WAS ALSO WRONG, IN OUR FAVOUR. *** The '~89 F_p multiplications per evaluation' figure assumed a witnessed A0. When A0 (or the line) is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT, x_A2, y_A2, the coefficients, the slope/intercept and every power x_i^t are constants, so evaluating a witnessed-coefficient polynomial at them is a FREE AFFINE FORM. Per line the only rows are the DIVISIONS: 3 (one per intersection point, common-denominator encoding) + 1 per basis point. n=1: ~6 mulmods/line, or ~9 with explicit nonzero certificates. 14 lines x 9 = ~126 certified F_p multiplications, against ~364 for the current 4-dim GLV lattice design.

*** WHY IT IS STILL NOT ACTIONABLE, AND THESE ARE THE BLOCKERS TO ATTACK IN ORDER. *** (1) The converse -- 'identity holds in b => (ep-en)P = Q' -- is Eagen's theorem and I could NOT fetch the paper (eprint 403). I verified only the forward direction numerically. Everything above prices a theorem we have not read. (2) Eagen's own notebook warns verbatim: 'if the scalars can exceed field length protocol can fail to be sound', and his demo uses scalars HALF the field length. Our ep, en are 251/255 bits on a 256-bit field. If the half-length restriction is real, GLV-split first: n=2, 18 lines, ~198 mulmods -- still under 364, so the lead survives either way. (3) ep and en enter the circuit as F_p elements but must be INTEGERS for the divisor argument, so they carry integer range obligations (ep-en = k holds over Z, verified: exactly, at 8/64/255 bits). (4) THE ACTUAL KILLER FOR THIS PIPELINE: the Lean soundness theorem would need Weil reciprocity, divisors and principality on an elliptic curve. Mathlib has the group law via the class group but nothing like the function-field machinery this needs. That is a multi-month formalisation, and Aristotle will not produce it. NEXT STEP, and it is cheap: get eprint 2022/596 by any route (author homepage, a mirror, a citing thesis) and read the soundness theorem's exact hypotheses. Everything else is priced.

*** NOW BACKED BY THE FORMAL LITERATURE, AND A SECOND DERANDOMISED ROUTE ALSO LOSES. *** The empirical finding here (single fixed A0 is surjective onto Q; 200/200 forgeries) matches Eagen eprint 2022/596 §1 verbatim: 'the prover must perform divisions in response to some random data chosen by the verifier', with §3.2 explaining that the x- and y-norms fail because 'the prover can tell ahead of time what points will map to the same roots of the norm' — a fixed Z is a fixed norm, same attack. Bassa/Veridise Theorem 10 gives error ~18N/q via the Dvir-Kollar-Lovett projective Schwartz-Zippel bound, and LEMMA 3 IS THE KILLER: for a FALSE statement there are still up to (2M-1)q+1 GOOD lines, so with the line fixed the prover chooses the false divisor second and the check degenerates to one scalar equation in O(k) free coefficients. Veridise's audit says it outright: 'A fixed random challenge was used. In particular, this does not prove anything about the interactive nature of the protocol.' The 7-constraint FCMP++ gadget is real but lives in Generalized Bulletproofs with a POST-COMMITMENT hash; Garaga Fiat-Shamirs with Poseidon252 over public inputs AND the prover's hint. Neither is available.

SECOND ROUTE, CHECKED AND ALSO NEGATIVE: check the norm identity p(x)^2 - (x^3+ax+b)q(x)^2 = c*prod_i(x - x_i) COEFFICIENT-WISE, which needs no challenge at all since coefficient matches are free affine. For n~256 ladder points that is one product tree over n linear factors (~1,983) plus two degree-n/2 squarings (~512) ~ 2,500 multiplications, EVERY ONE NON-NATIVE at ~214 each, so ~534,000 against our 303,948 record. leads.summary: Deterministic permutation / multiset-equality certificate with NO random challenge: a Waksman network of 1-row switches. Cost 2(n log2 n - n + 1) score. n=64 -> 642, n=1024 -> 18434.

THE SWITCH IS THE NEW PART AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING ON ITS OWN. The textbook selector out1 = a + s(b-a) with s boolean costs 2 rows + 2 witnesses. Instead witness ONLY out1 and assert (out1 - a)(out1 - b) = 0, then take out2 = a + b - out1 as a free affine. That pins {out1,out2} = {a,b} as a MULTISET in one row and one witness. NOTHING IN THE CURRENT FIVE CHALLENGES NEEDS THIS. Recorded because it is the correct answer to sorting, RAM, and set-equality if one ever appears, and because the 1-row two-root switch is a I.4-family gadget (decoy roots) we did not have.

*** THREE CORRECTIONS FROM THE CERTIFICATES RESEARCH PASS, 2026-08-12, AND THE FIRST IS A SOUNDNESS BUG. ***

(1) *** THE TWO-ROOT SWITCH DOES NOT COMPOSE FOR MULTI-LIMB ITEMS. *** The two-root row (O-U)(O-V) = 0 carries NO CONTROL BIT. Route a w-limb item by running w independent switches and you have proved only PER-LIMB multiset preservation: limb 0 may go left while limb 1 goes right, and the items are SHREDDED. This is a correctness defect, not an inefficiency, and it applies to the switch1row result the moment the payload is wider than one field element. libsnark's answer is a boolean selector at 2w+1 constraints and w+1 allocations per switch (~3w+2 score). *** THE FIX IS BETTER THAN THE FALLBACK: lambda-PACK THE ITEM AND ROUTE THE PACKED VALUE. *** With X = sum_j x_j lambda^j (a FREE affine form), one row (O-U)(O-V) = 0 pins the WHOLE item and the sibling output U+V-O stays free. Packing is injective on already-range-checked limbs whenever sum_j (2^b - 1) lambda^j < p, i.e. w*b <= 253. Measured: 128-bit item 14/switch -> 2/switch (7x); 256-bit 26 -> 4 (6.5x, two packs under the 253-bit cap); single field element 5 -> 2. At n=256 items of 256 bits that is 1,793 switches * 4 = 7,172 against libsnark's 46,618. Keep every wire inside the network packed and unpack only at the boundary.

(2) THE COST FORMULA IN THIS ENTRY IS WRONG OFF POWERS OF TWO. 2(n log2 n - n + 1) is exact ONLY for n = 2^k. The AS-Waksman recurrence W(n) = W(floor(n/2)) + W(ceil(n/2)) + n - 1 has closed form W(n) = n*ceil(log2 n) - 2^ceil(log2 n) + 1 = sum_{i=1}^n ceil(log2 i), verified against the recurrence for all n <= 5000. At n = 100 that is 573, not 565 — we would UNDER-BUDGET. Also DO NOT PAD TO A POWER OF TWO: n=100 native is 573 switches against 769 padded, a 34% penalty.

(3) THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING LEFT IN THE NETWORK ITSELF. The information-theoretic lower bound is log2(n!) and AS-Waksman is within +25 at n=64 and +447 at n=1024 — about 3% off optimal. Do not look for a better network; look at the payload encoding (item 1) instead.

leads.summary: n-ary XOR of booleans: for n >= 7 extract the parity from the FREE sum instead of building an XOR3 tree. Witness the m = ceil(log2(floor(n/2)+1)) bits of q, assert (s-2q)(s-2q-1) = 0; parity is the free affine s-2q. Cost 2m+1 vs 2*ceil((n-1)/2).
leads.note: Crossover is at n=7 (tree 6 vs free-sum 5); it widens fast -- n=15 gives 14 vs 7, n=31 gives 30 vs 9, n=63 gives 62 vs 11. Linear becomes logarithmic. SOUNDNESS: q is a genuine integer in [0, 2^m - 1] via its own bits, and s - 2q in {0,1} forces q = floor(s/2) uniquely; a superset range is safe whenever 2q+1 > n is unreachable. NOT APPLICABLE TO KECCAK THETA -- its widest XOR is the 5-way column parity, which is below the crossover, and see keccak-theta-slp for why materialising anything wider loses. The general form is Paterson-Stockmeyer: any SYMMETRIC boolean function is a univariate in the free sum s, evaluable in about 2*sqrt(n) products (m non-scalar mults reach degree floor((m+2)^2/4)). Look for symmetric subfunctions before building trees. NEGATIVE WORTH KEEPING: generic bit-packing into base-8/base-13 digits of one field element never helps, because the unpacking identity was ALREADY free and packing forces you to witness digits that were free affine forms. Carries cannot be shared across words -- each W feeds exactly one sigma0 and one sigma1 in its lifetime and the majority words of different steps have disjoint variable sets. leads.summary: CLOSED DIRECTIONS, recorded so they are not re-explored. Sparse/spread representation, meet-in-the-middle, alternative rotation-friendly representations, and rank/tensor diagonalisation of the Sigma words are all dead, each for a structural reason.
leads.note: (1) SPARSE/SPREAD (halo2 table16, 2099 rows) -- the ENTIRE saving is that the dense<->spread bijection is one LOOKUP row. Enforcing it arithmetically means decomposing the 16-bit chunk into bits and re-summing with weights 4^i, i.e. back to >=1 row per bit. No lookup-free variant exists or can. (2) MEET-IN-THE-MIDDLE -- the backward round invokes the IDENTICAL four nonlinear gadgets on the identical words; the bijection is realised entirely by free affine rearrangement, so direction does not touch the nonlinear content. Zero gain, and note the feed-forward is NOT what blocks it. (3) ROTATION-FRIENDLY REPRESENTATIONS (roots of unity in F_r, F_2[x]/(x^32-1)) -- every invertible linear change of representation is free in BOTH directions, so it cannot change the cost of anything. The bit vector already has rotation free AND addition free; the only cost is re-decomposition, which is intrinsic to the nonlinear interface. (4) RANK/TENSOR DIAGONALISATION of the Sigma words -- the quadratic part is rank <= 32 and would give 16 rows, but the cubic part T = sum 2^j x_{j+u} x_{j+v} x_{j+w} is a DIAGONAL 3-tensor with 32 nonzero entries, slice rank exactly 32, so >= ceil(32/3) = 11 multiplications for T alone and realistically 32. THE LESSON: the non-vanishing-multiplier row is extraordinarily good precisely because it computes a degree-3 function in ONE row by hiding the degree in a division. Rank methods must pay for degree 3 explicitly and cannot compete. (5) A GENUINE BUT SMALL ITEM, not a dead end: for the FIRST block the state is the constant IV, so round 0's gadgets are compile-time constants and at round 1 both Maj and Ch have two constant arguments and collapse to free affine functions. Worth about 2 rounds on block 1 only.

leads.summary: The grand-product permutation argument IS derandomisable without a challenge, and the naive way to do it is quadratic while the right way is n*log2(n) - n/4 - 1 products.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11 in the verification-identities pass; libsnark AS-Waksman sources fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com; Newton's identities and Shurman's resultant notes fetched.
leads.note: prod_i(a_i+g) = prod_i(b_i+g) with g fixed is ONE equation in n free unknowns -> the prover solves for b_n -> VACUOUS, exactly the Wesolowski disease. But both sides are monic of degree n in g, so the difference has degree <= n-1 and checking at n DISTINCT FIXED points forces the identity unconditionally. The trap: evaluating prod_i(x_j - b_i) separately at each of n points costs n^2-n products. The fix: build the product by a BINARY TREE, and at each node multiply two monic degree-d polynomials by the 2d+1-fixed-point evaluate/multiply/interpolate route (evaluation of a witnessed-coefficient polynomial at a compile-time point is a FREE affine form; only the pointwise products are rows). Naive convolution wins for d<=2, evaluation for d>=3, giving C(n) = n*log2(n) - n/4 - 1 products; verified by direct recursion at n=4..1024 (C(8)=21, C(16)=59, C(64)=367, C(256)=1983). Score against a PUBLIC multiset = 2n*log2(n) - n/2 - 4; both sides witnessed = 4n*log2(n) - n - 8. Compare Waksman with libsnark's boolean-ELIMINATED switch (o1-u)(o1-v)=0 (1 row, 1 alloc, NOT the 2-row boolean form): 2(n*log2(n) - n + 1), about 15% cheaper. Two unrelated derandomisations landing on the same 2n*log2(n) is good evidence that is the true price of a challenge-free permutation. The product tree is much easier to prove in Lean (one Vandermonde uniqueness lemma + a tree induction) than Waksman's routability.

leads.summary: Rows are charged per multiplication and nothing else, so the row count of any bilinear map is its TENSOR RANK. Strassen is therefore a free lunch in R1CS with crossover at n=2, not n~100.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11; Strassen exponent and Winograd addition counts fetched from Wikipedia.
leads.note:
Every non-multiplicative step of a bilinear algorithm -- the block adds, the change of basis, the reassembly -- is affine and therefore FREE, so the R1CS cost of a bilinear map is exactly its bilinear rank. Same theorem as the Winograd 2n-k bound for F[u]/P already in CIRCONOMICON I.10, stated for the matrix-multiplication tensor. Consequence: n^3 -> 7^log2(n). n=8: 512 -> 343 (33%); n=16: 4096 -> 2401 (41%); n=64: 262144 -> 117649 (55%). Each leaf product is (affine form in A) x (affine form in B), a legal rank-1 row. The numerical-stability and addition-overhead objections that push Strassen's classical crossover to n~100 are all costs this model does not charge. Laderman R(3,3,3)<=23 and AlphaTensor-style decompositions would push further -- UNVERIFIED, not fetched, do not quote numbers without a decomposition in hand.

*** SETTLED IN LEAN, AND THE HEADLINE CLAIM IN THIS ENTRY IS TOO STRONG. *** Aristotle research job `bilinearrank` (collected 2026-08-12), research_out/bilinearrank/bilinearrank_aristotle/Solution/Research/, zero errors, no `sorry`, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. *** IT IS AN INEQUALITY, NOT AN EQUALITY — and the useful direction is the one that holds. *** `rows_le_rank : minRows f ≤ tensorRank f` over any field: a rank-r decomposition becomes r rows verbatim, so Strassen-style savings DO transfer and this entry's practical advice stands. But the converse is only quadratic: `rank_le_nine_rows_sq : tensorRank f ≤ 9 * (minRows f)^2`. So row count is NOT the tensor rank, and a tensor-rank LOWER bound does NOT give a row-count lower bound of the same size — do not use rank lower bounds to argue a row count is optimal. The model charges one row per product with A, B, C arbitrary linear forms on the WHOLE witness (nothing restricted to bilinear shape), Complete = some witness satisfies, Sound = every satisfying witness gives the right output. THE HARD DIRECTION IS ALSO DONE, at one row: `minRows_le_one_iff_rank_le_one` over an infinite field, hence `two_le_minRows_of_two_le_rank` — rank >= 2 forces >= 2 rows, with the row left completely unrestricted (OneRow.lean, ~530 lines).

*** A THIRD CORRECTION, AND IT CLOSES A SEARCH THIS ENTRY WAS INVITING. *** This entry asks whether nondeterminism beats computation for bilinear maps. Kunnemann, 'On Nondeterministic Derandomization of Freivalds' Algorithm', ESA 2018 (arXiv:1806.09189): whether n x n matrix multiplication can be VERIFIED in near-optimal nondeterministic time O~(n^2) is a NAMED OPEN PROBLEM in fine-grained complexity, and sufficiently fast deterministic verifiers for it would follow from deterministic univariate polynomial identity testing. So (a) stop hunting for a nondeterministic shortcut to matrix or limb products — finding one would resolve an open problem; (b) FREIVALDS ITSELF IS A HARD NEGATIVE HERE: with r fixed the adversary picks AB - C having r in its kernel, and derandomising needs n independent vectors, which IS the full product; (c) Strassen-style rank reduction remains the only real lever, exactly as the Lean rows_le_rank says.

leads.summary: A chi output bit costs ONE R1CS row with output booleanity FREE, and a 3-way parity costs ONE row. That is theta 2240 rows (not 6400) and chi 5 rows per 5-bit row (not 10).
leads.source: Derived and machine-verified over BN254 F_r 2026-08-11; Keccak reference v3.0 fetched from keccak.team/files/Keccak-reference-3.0.pdf.
leads.note:
