So two independent routes agree on the construction, and the 122,880 kec-port-record item is not just a copy job -- its target is now confirmed optimal-in-family by a derivation that never saw it.
THE ACTION IS UNCHANGED: this is already queued as the port ladder, Rung A (ChiLane alone, -76,800) then Rung B then Rung C. Do NOT open a separate line of work on it.

chi: (4a'_i - 3a_i + a_{i+1} + a_{i+2}) * (2a_i - 2a_{i+1} - 2a_{i+2} + 1) = 3a_i - a_{i+1} - 5a_{i+2}. The right factor takes values in {1,-1,-1,-3,3,1,1,-1} on the cube -- NEVER ZERO -- so a'_i is uniquely pinned to a boolean and its booleanity costs 0. Verified on all 8 inputs. Needs char not in {2,3}. parity-of-3: (2o - s)(2s - 3) = -s with s = x+y+z, right factor in {-3,-1,1,3}. parity-of-2: (o + 2s)(s + 1) = 6s. The parity-3 gadget works for ANY affine form provably valued in [0,3], so parity cost rho(k) = min(ceil(log2(k+1)), 1 + rho(k-2)); crossover at k=7. THETA REBUILT: share the column parities. C[x][z] = parity of 5 -> 2 rows, 320*2 = 640; then each output bit = parity of 3 -> 1 row, 1600. Total 2240 rows/theta, 2.9x under the naive 4-rows-per-bit 6400. Full Keccak-f1600 budget on this basis: 1600 + 24*2240 + 24*1600 = 93,760 rows = 93,760 allocs, score ~187,520. CHECK THIS AGAINST THE LIVE TREE BEFORE SPENDING A SLOT -- it may already be in.
INVERSES ARE DEAD, with the reason: computed theta and theta^-1 over GF(2) by Gauss-Jordan -- EVERY row of theta has weight exactly 11, EVERY row of theta^-1 has weight exactly 851 (density 0.5319), confirming the Keccak reference's 'Hamming weight of the polynomial of theta^-1 is of the order b/2'. 16,000 rows vs 2240, 7.1x worse. chi^-1 = a'_i XOR (~a'_{i+1} AND (a'_{i+2} XOR (~a'_{i+3} AND a'_{i+4}))) = two chi-shaped layers, F_r multilinear degree 5, and it provably admits NO one-row certificate (the required cofactor is forced to a multiple of a'_{i+1}, which vanishes on the cube) -> 10 rows, exactly 2x. AND MEET-IN-THE-MIDDLE IS A NO-OP, NOT A LOSS: R1CS asserts a relation, not a function; witnessing a midpoint and 'running backward' emits character-for-character the same constraints. Inversion pays only when a component is expensive forward and cheap backward; Keccak has no such component.

leads.summary: Composing two SHA-256 rounds saves EXACTLY ZERO (788 = 788), and folding the message schedule's carries COSTS 39. Both closed with explicit counts.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11; circomlib ch.circom and sha256compression.circom fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com; verified against real 2-round SHA-256 on 2000 random states.
leads.note: TWO-ROUND COMPOSITION: 2 rounds separately = <392,396> = 788. Composed, including every obligation the composition still forces = <392,396> = 788. IDENTICAL. Reason, and it generalises: E = e_{t+1} and A = a_{t+1} are the ARGUMENTS OF BITWISE MAPS (Sigma1/Ch read E bitwise, Sigma0/Maj read A bitwise), so their 32-bit decompositions are mandatory however you write the relation. Composition raises the symbolic degree but R1CS caps every row at degree 2, so flattening puts back exactly the rows composition removed. Composition here is anti-flattening followed by an undo. a_{t+1} - e_{t+1} = T2_t - d_t IS affine and true mod 2^32 (verified) but is LITERALLY R2 - R1 of the two reduction relations -- linearly dependent, zero new information, and materialising T1 to 'exploit the sharing' costs +63/round. The GF(2) AND-count rewrites INVERT SIGN over F_r: Ch = g^(e&(f^g)) is <3,3>/bit against <1,1>/bit for g + e(f-g); Maj = (a&b)^(c&(a^b)) is <4,4>/bit against <1,1>/bit for the MAJ3 row. 3x and 4x worse -- do not port AND-count results into this model. MESSAGE SCHEDULE: the generating-function collapse dies twice -- sigma0 is not multiplication by any constant of F_r (the rotate's wraparound depends on the low bits), and a truncated power-series identity is 48 coefficient equations, collapsing which is Schwartz-Zippel. The carry fold: |R_t| < 2^34 so B = 2^35, and 35m - 1 < 253.597 gives EXACTLY 7 steps foldable per relation. But it LOSES: the per-step linking relation is already a ring identity costing 0 rows, and each independent linear relation is worth exactly one free derived witness, so folding 46 relations into 7 costs +39 allocations and saves 0 rows. 8650 -> 8689. ALSO: CIRCONOMICON I.2 claims 128 score per round pair for lambda-packing; only 64 (the Ch pair) could be substantiated -- Maj provably does not pack in the I.2 shape (surviving degree-3 ANF terms) and an exhaustive integer search over the I.1 shape (759,375 candidates) came back empty. POSSIBLE OVER-CLAIM IN OUR OWN NOTES -- re-derive before relying on it.

leads.summary: Additive folding works at the LIMB level, not the relation level, and only after the limb products are replaced by a 2k-1-point FIXED-evaluation check. Worth 39.6% per modmul. Everything multiplicative dies.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11 with exact integer bit budgets; xJsnark PDF (akosba.github.io/papers/xjsnark.pdf) and gnark std/math/emulated/field_mul.go fetched.
leads.note:
KEEP TWO SOUNDNESS ARGUMENTS STRICTLY APART. (L) magnitude lift: U = V mod r plus |U|,|V| < r/2 gives U = V over Z -- a no-wraparound argument, NOT Schwartz-Zippel, and every use needs an explicit bit budget. (V) Vandermonde: two polynomials of degree <= D agreeing at D+1 FIXED distinct public points are identical -- deterministic, zero soundness error. gnark's mulCheck uses the FORBIDDEN thing (its own comment: 'checked only at a single random point', challenge from a commitment) -- unusable here. xJsnark uses (V): 'For each c in {1..2m-1}, the circuit checks (sum x[i]c^i)(sum y[i]c^i) = sum z[i]c^i ... total number of constraints is 2m-1'. That is the purest form of check-don't-compute and it is legal.
DEAD: multiplicative telescoping (k folded squarings need a quotient of ~4096*2^k bits; k=16 is 268,431,361 bits, and the optimum is k=1 -- enforced at k=2 not by the quotient, which is a literal tie at 16,385 vs 16,386 bits, but by the limb-product count, 1.82x worse). DEAD: relation-level additive folding (residuals are 8193 bits, B > 2^8194, and floor(254/8194) = 0 relations fold -- you would need a 139,281-bit field). DEAD: RNS/CRT auxiliary moduli (1.85x worse; a CRT modulus certifies ~111 bits at 2.5 score/bit while a positional fold chunk certifies b*g bits at 0.25 score/bit, because the carry is NARROWER than the window it certifies while the RNS quotient is WIDER than its modulus; and Mersenne moduli are impossible -- the primes up to 126 sum to 1,593 bits < 8,194).
ALIVE: overlapping-weight limb folding, g_max(b) = floor((252 - ceil(lg k) - 2)/b) - 1. b=64 folds exactly 2, b=20 folds 11. Combined optimum b=20, k=205, g=11: 20,132 score/modmul against 33,351, a 39.6% saving, chain 342,244. AND THE LOAD-BEARING WARNING: for an ARBITRARY residual vector every chunk equation is satisfiable mod p by C_j = S_j * (2^{bg})^{-1}, with forged carries 250-253 bits wide -- the chunk rows are VACUOUS on their own and the entire soundness content is the 28-bit carry RANGE CHECK. Any fold without a bound is unsound. RESIDUE: 278,562 of the final 342,244 (81.4%) is range checks on q and t, at a provable 2 score/bit for the whole digit-decomposition family (one row at most doubles degree, so d bits need >= d rows; the base-4 gadget (y^2-y)(y^2-5y+6)=0 ties booleanity, it does not beat it). A sub-2-score-per-bit range argument is worth more than every structural trick above combined.

leads.summary: Elliptic nets / division polynomials / Somos lose to windowed fixed-base double-and-add by 20-30x, and a fixed base buys them ~0%. Closed with sourced numbers. Pairings on secp256k1 are not merely expensive, they are not representable.
leads.source: Stange thesis (katestange.net/colorado/papers/Stange-Thesis-Brown2008.pdf) and EDS formulary (katestange.net/colorado/papers/edsformulary.pdf) FETCHED and quoted; counts reproduced by an operation-counting implementation checked against real secp256k1 scalar multiplication.
leads.note: Real per-bit cost is 22M + 6S + 4 const-M (Stange's own optimised block algorithm, thesis 18.4), rising to 24M + 6S + 4 const-M + 8 selects in-circuit because the scalar is secret -- 2-3x worse than the 12-16/bit folklore figure. Cross-checks against her Table 18.1. The 8-term block (thesis Thm 19.2.5) is provably minimal: width b supports b-4 values of i giving 2(b-4) new terms, and 2b-8 >= b forces b >= 8. Point recovery x(kP) = x(P) - W(k-1)W(k+1)/W(k)^2 and y(kP) = (W(k+2)W(k-1)^2 - W(k-2)W(k+1)^2)/(4y(P)W(k)^3), ~13 mulmods once, negligible. FIXED BASE BUYS NOTHING: only the initial block and the 4 constant multipliers are compile-time; the block after t steps depends on the whole t-bit prefix, so nothing downstream is constant, and precomputing 2^t initial blocks needs a 2^t-way decoder that eats the gain. Stange's own escape -- 'if W(2,0) has a cube root nu in F_q ... saving four F_q multiplications per iteration' -- is UNAVAILABLE on secp256k1: p = 1 mod 3 and 2*y_G is not a cube mod p (checked). TOTALS: 255 steps x 34 mulmod-equivalents ~ 8,200-8,700 mulmods ~ 41k-70k rows, against ~2,200-2,700 rows for 4-bit-window fixed-base affine addition (63 additions x 3 certified mulmods -- note the affine add is 3, not 5: lam*(x2-x1) = y2-y1, lam*lam = x3+x1+x2, lam*(x1-x3) = y3+y1, all RHS affine and free). 0.75 mulmods/bit against 34. Nets are inherently bit-serial -- Stange, thesis 18.4: 'A triple-and-add adaptation ... does not seem promising, by the nature of the recurrence relation.' Division polynomials are the SAME algorithm (W_n = lambda^(n^2-1) psi_n) with the same count; Somos-4 is the same sequence reached by an O(n) traversal. All three dead. EMBEDDING DEGREE of secp256k1 = ord_n(p) = (n-1)/6 = 254 bits exactly (computed and minimality-checked against every prime divisor of k). F_{p^k} has ~5e78 bits. Pairings do not exist in any computational sense -- every pairing-based verification identity is dead on arrival.

leads.summary: With a deterministic verifier, dIP = NP: there is no protocol to find, only an NP certificate to golf. The right literature is CERTIFYING ALGORITHMS, not SNARKs. Prefer certificates whose verification condition is LINEAR, because linear is free.
leads.source: Katz, Notes on Complexity Theory Lecture 16 (cs.umd.edu/~jkatz/complexity/f11/lecture16.pdf) and Mehlhorn, Certifying Algorithms slides (people.mpi-inf.mpg.de/~mehlhorn/ftp/CertifyingAlgs.pdf), both FETCHED and quoted. The McConnell-Mehlhorn-Naeher-Schweitzer CSR 2011 survey full text could NOT be fetched -- bibliographic data only, treat page numbers as unverified.
leads.note: Katz, verbatim: 'if the verifier is deterministic then the prover can predict all the verifier's questions in advance, and simply include all the corresponding answers as part of the (static) proof.' Our Lean obligation IS a deterministic verifier. So sumcheck, GKR, PCP, KZG, Bulletproofs, plookup/logUp, Wesolowski/Pietrzak are all dead as protocols and useful only as sources of algebraic identities to be derandomised at deg+1 fixed points. THE PATTERN WORTH INTERNALISING is Farkas: the certificate for a NO answer is often a linear functional, and linear functionals are free. Non-solvability of Ax=b is witnessed by c with c^T A = 0 (n^2 FREE affine equations) and c^T b != 0 (one nonzero-certificate row) -- 2 rows total. Same shape for LP infeasibility, min-cut, and Koenig's |M| = |C|. 2-colourability of a compile-time graph is <n,n> regardless of |E| because b_u + b_v - 1 = 0 is affine. Planarity via f - e + n = 2 is a counting identity, i.e. affine, i.e. free. THE DETERMINANT HIERARCHY, worth knowing before paying: det A = 0 costs n^2 (a null vector); det A != 0 costs n^{log2 7} (witness B, assert AB = I -- one-sided suffices over a field, do not pay for both); det A = d costs (n^3-n)/3 + n - 1 (witnessed LU). Ask which you need. NOTE A*adj(A) = d*I is NOT a valid certificate for det A = d -- with the adjugate free it only gives det A * det B = d^n, which fails the vacuity test. RANK EXACTLY r without index selection: A = XY (rank <= r) AND UAV = I_r (rank >= r, since rank(UAV) <= rank(A)); dodges the one-hot decodes a named minor would cost. SQUARE ROOT, the sharpest single lesson: s*s = x is 1 row and a ~380x win when you do not care WHICH root, and a NET LOSS when you do -- pinning the canonical root needs a canonical bit-decomposition plus a comparison against (r-1)/2, ~760 score, more than the ~380 rows of just exponentiating. And if BOTH s and x are free witnesses the check says only 'x is a square' -- that is the vacuous configuration. LEGENDRE SYMBOL in 4 rows: b(b-1) = 0, x*u = 1, t = x*(1 + b*(nu-1)), s*s = t with nu a compile-time non-residue; exactly one of b = 0, b = 1 is satisfiable, so b is forced. The x*u = 1 row is not optional -- without it x = 0 admits both. ORDER IS NEVER ALGEBRAIC: every <, min, sorted, median costs a range check, and witnessing only moves WHICH value gets range-checked, never how many bits. Sorting networks are strictly dominated by log2(n)^2/4 -- witness the sorted array, certify the permutation, pay n-1 comparisons instead of (n/4)log^2(n) of them (n=64,k=32: 4,611 against 36,864). ELIMINATION, the cross-cutting rule and its exception: in R1CS intermediate witnesses are CHEAP (alloc + row = 2, flat) and eliminating them RAISES DEGREE, which is the opposite of the classical instinct. Resultants multiply degrees (Shurman: the resultant is homogeneous of degree mn in the roots), so eliminating n variables from degree-d relations gives degree ~d^n. Chain of monomials: a wash. Boolean selector: elimination WINS -- y = b*u + (1-b)*v costs 4, while (y-u)(y-v) = 0 costs 1, and generally y in {c_1..c_k} for compile-time constants is k-1 rows and 0 allocations against >= 2k. Branching chain: elimination is a DISASTER, 4n against Omega(2^n). Rule: eliminate a boolean selector, never eliminate through a chain.
